title: Audit readiness playbook: RBAC to SIEM
body:
Purpose:
This one-page playbook is a concise, customer-facing checklist and mapping guide to help security teams prepare for audits when migrating from legacy RBAC to RBAC v2 and enabling SIEM export and evidence automation. It is written for compliance owners, platform engineers, and SOC teams who need clear artifacts and queries to show auditors.

Executive summary:
- RBAC v2 introduces scoped principals, attribute-based grants, and richer role metadata.
- Audit logs include expanded fields (role_id, grant_reason, session_attrs) required for traceability.
- SIEM export supports JSON line ingestion or syslog with gzip and TLS.
- Evidence automation bundles artifact snapshots, signed audit excerpts, and reproducible queries for customer review.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Hosted and Dedicated deployments. Private (on-prem) may require local SIEM connectors.
- Assumes customer has an existing SIEM (Splunk, Elastic, SumoLogic, or Microsoft Sentinel) and can accept HTTPS or syslog ingestion.
- Focused on authentication/authorization events, role changes, escalation, and data-access audit events.

What changed in RBAC v2 (high level):
- Roles are namespaced: role.namespace + role.name (supports cross-tenant delegation).
- Grants can be time-limited and context-aware (ip_range, device_id).
- Role bindings are first-class objects with history and reason metadata.
- UI/API now surfaces binding IDs that map directly to audit events.

Minimum audit fields (summarized - present in exported schema):
- timestamp: RFC3339 string
- event_id: UUID
- actor: { actor_type, actor_id, actor_email } (flattened fields in export: actor_type, actor_id, actor_email)
- action: canonical action name (e.g., role.bind, role.unbind, token.exchange, model.invoke)
- resource: resource_type and resource_id (e.g., model, dataset, endpoint)
- role_id, role_name, role_namespace
- grant_id, grant_reason, grant_ttl_seconds
- session_id, session_attrs (ip, ua, mfa_used)
- outcome: success | failure | denied
- request_id and request_path for request tracing
- raw_payload: optional base64 of raw request for repro (access-controlled)

Notes on export formats and SIEM ingest:
- Preferred: JSON-lines over HTTPS with HMAC-signed batch header.
- Alternative: syslog/tcp with TLS and batching; ensure newline-delimited JSON per message.
- Compression: gzip allowed for daily bulk export only. Real-time streams must be uncompressed.
- Envelope header fields: source=redwood, env=prod|staging, region=us-west-2 (useful for SIEM parsers).

Suggested SIEM parsers / example queries (customer-ready):
- Splunk (search): index=redwood sourcetype=rbac_logs action=role.bind OR action=role.unbind | stats count by actor_email, role_name, outcome
- Elastic KQL: event.dataset:rbac AND (action:role.bind or action:role.unbind) | group by actor_email, role_name
- Sentinel (KQL): RBACLogs | where action in ("role.bind","role.unbind") | summarize count() by actor_email, role_name, bin(timestamp, 1d)
- Quick escalation detection: where action=="role.bind" and grant_ttl_seconds>86400 and actor_email not in (admin@company.com)

Evidence automation bundle (what we provide):
- snapshot/audit_log_sample.jsonl (redacted, signed) — 7 days of representative events covering binds/unbinds, failed auth, and data-access.
- roles_export.csv — current role definitions and namespaces with creation/update timestamps.
- bindings_history.csv — chronological binding changes with grant_reason and admin reviewer.
- verification_script.sh — small helper that runs a set of queries (Splunk/Elastic templates) against customer SIEM endpoints to demonstrate reproducibility.
- proofs_of_delivery.md — signed delivery manifest for artifact chain-of-custody.

Customer prerequisites checklist (short):
- SIEM endpoint reachable and ingestion credentials provided (HTTPS or TLS syslog).
- List of customer admin emails to be whitelisted for detection rules.
- Decision on retention window (recommended min 90 days for role bindings; 365 days for escalations).
- Agreement on redaction policy for PII fields in sample exports.
- Point of contact for audit day and SOC liaison.

Migration and audit rollout steps (recommended timeline):
1) Discovery (1 week): inventory current roles, bindings, and key resources.
2) Mapping (1 week): map legacy roles to RBAC v2 namespaces and identify gaps.
3) Dry-run export (3 days): enable SIEM export to a staging index, run parsing templates.
4) Pilot (2 weeks): enable RBAC v2 for a low-risk tenant, collect evidence, adjust alerts.
5) Audit readiness validation (3 days): produce evidence bundle and run verification_script.sh with customer SOC.
6) Rollout and monitoring (2–4 weeks): full migration with daily digest and rollback hooks.
7) Post-audit retention adjustment and automation tuning (ongoing).

Rollbacks and mitigations:
- RBAC v2 changes are additive; we provide an API to reverse binds by grant_id.
- If SIEM parsers fail, revert to staging export and ship last-known-good parser.
- We keep immutable daily archives for 30 days to support rollback forensic queries.

Common auditor questions we prep answers for (examples):
- How do you prove who granted a role and why? -> binding_history.csv with grant_reason and reviewer fields + signed audit sample.
- Can you show a reproducible query that surfaces privilege escalation? -> provide the Splunk/Sentinel templates above plus a README.
- How is the log integrity protected? -> HMAC-signed batches and TLS for in-transit protection; notarized delivery manifest.

Contacts and next steps:
- Customer SOC onboarding: Marcus Chen (marcus@redwood.ai)
- Compliance lead: Anjali Rao (anjali@redwood.ai)
- Telemetry engineering (for custom fields): Dmitri Volkov (dmitri@redwood.ai)

Appendix: minimal SIEM field mapping (flat export names):
- ts, event_id, actor_type, actor_id, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, role_namespace, role_name, role_id, grant_id, grant_reason, grant_ttl_seconds, session_id, session_ip, session_ua, outcome, request_id, request_path, raw_payload_b64

Document notes: this playbook is intentionally concise for customer security reviews. For an expanded version (with sample exports and parser code) see CONFLUENCE-1254 and github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-config.
